newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican peso closes higher on Cetes hike forecast.
newsitem.headline: Mexican peso closes higher on Cetes hike forecast.

text.p: The stumbling Mexican peso fought its way back to positive turf in the closing minutes of trade on Tuesday after receiving a helping hand from the prospect of soaring primary interest rates, traders said.

"They say Cetes hikes will be hefty at this evening's auction. That stemmed the flow of foreigners who were stepping out of Mexico and made banks sell dollars to buy money market paper," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 1.1 and one centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.7190/7.7290 and 7.7150/7.7250.
The same-day peso earlier closed 13.2 centavos weaker at 7.7250/7.7350 per dollar, after not having traded since Friday.
Money market traders surveyed by Reuters meanwhile expected bellwether 28-day Cetes rates to increase by an average of 371 basis points to 26.45 percent at Tuesday's Banco de Mexico auction.
"I have my doubts about how investors will take to such a sharp hike in Cetes rates," a trader said. "At times such jolts are counterproductive for the (financial) markets."
Traders estimated that primary Cetes hikes could hold the peso steady on Wednesday.
